wins.label: Strong Revenue Growth
wins.evidence: 2025 was a defining year for AMD with record revenue, net income and free cash flow driven by broad-based demand for our high-performance computing and AI products.

wins.label: Data Center Momentum
wins.evidence: Data Center segment revenue increased 39% year-over-year to a record $5.4 billion, led by accelerating Instinct MI350 Series GPU deployments and server share gains.

wins.label: EPYC Leadership
wins.evidence: EPYC has become the processor of choice for the modern data center, delivering leadership performance, efficiency and TCO.

wins.label: AI Software Expansion
wins.evidence: We expanded the ROCm ecosystem in the fourth quarter, enabling customers to deploy Instinct faster and with higher performance across a broader range of workloads.

wins.label: Future Product Roadmap
wins.evidence: Our next-generation Venice CPU extends our leadership across each of these metrics. Customer pull for Venice is very high with engagements underway to support large-scale cloud deployments.

risks.label: China Market Uncertainty
risks.evidence: We are not forecasting any additional revenue from China just because it's a very dynamic situation.

risks.label: Supply Chain Constraints
risks.evidence: We are working with our supply chain partners to increase supply as well. But from what we see today, I think the overall server situation is strong, and we are increasing supply to address that.

risks.label: Seasonal Decline in Client and Gaming
risks.evidence: We expect fourth quarter non-GAAP gross margin to be approximately 55%. Non-GAAP operating expense to be approximately $3.05 billion.

risks.label: Memory Inflation
risks.evidence: Based on everything that we see today, we're probably seeing the PC TAM down a bit just given some of the inflationary pressures of the commodities pricing, including memory.

risks.label: Competitive Pressure
risks.evidence: There is a great need for high-performance CPUs right now. And that goes towards agentic workloads where when you have these AI processes or AI agents that are spinning off a lot of work.

wins.label: Record Revenue & Profitability
wins.evidence: 2025 saw record revenue of $34.6 billion, up 34% year-over-year, and record net income of $2.5 billion, up 42%.

wins.label: Strong Data Center Growth
wins.evidence: Data Center segment revenue grew 39% year-over-year to a record $5.4 billion, driven by Instinct MI350 Series GPU deployments and server share gains.

wins.label: EPYC Dominance in Server Market
wins.evidence: Fifth-gen EPYC turn CPUs accounted for more than half of the total server revenue, and we exited the year with record server CPU sales to both cloud and enterprise customers.

wins.label: Expanding Instinct Adoption
wins.evidence: 8 of the top 10 AI companies use Instinct to power production workloads, and MI350 Series availability expanded significantly.

wins.label: ROCm Ecosystem Expansion
wins.evidence: Millions of large language and multimodal models run out of the box on AMD with the leading models launching with day zero support for Instinct GPUs.

risks.label: Memory Supply Constraints
risks.evidence: Analysts express concern about potential bottlenecks in memory supply impacting the ramp of recallable systems.

risks.label: PC Market Slowdown
risks.evidence: Expectation of a sequential decline in Client and Gaming revenue due to a potential slowdown in the PC market.

risks.label: Competition in AI Accelerators
risks.evidence: Competitor's development of KV cache offload and ASIC-style compute poses a competitive challenge.

risks.label: 7th Year of Console Cycle
risks.evidence: Semi-custom SoC revenue is expected to decline significantly in 2026 as AMD enters the seventh year of the current console cycle.

risks.label: Uncertainty in China Market
risks.evidence: Limited forecasting for MI308 sales in China due to ongoing regulatory uncertainties.
